| [QUESTION-281](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md) | By which dynamical transitions do the distinctions individuation needs come into being and pass away (instability that amplifies small differences, nucleation across a finite barrier from a locally stable state, bifurcation of the set of attractors, noise- or rate-induced tipping), and are a form's creation, its stabilization and its coming to have a constitutive role three separate achievements? | The owner's U14 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "does this elucidate other work we should account for? maybe in the neighborhood of dynamics? bifurcation/catastrophe theory? far from equilibrium dynamics? pattern formation?" It ended on "the mechanisms that create a form, the mechanisms that stabilize it, and the mechanisms through which it acquires a constitutive or autonomous role. The record's individuation claims say when a form is one system and how long it lasts ([QUESTION-035](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md)); none says how it begins or ends. | [QUESTION-287](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-287.md) | In a deterministic singularly perturbed system whose eliminated variable is fast and contracting and whose reduced system is contracting, does the memoryless quasi-steady-state reduction predict the coarse variable with an error bounded uniformly in time in terms of the eliminated dynamics? | The fast contracting case of [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-773](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-773.md) (Active) settles it. No memory coordinate is needed: the reduction on the slow manifold stays within O(ε) of the true slow trajectory for all t ≥ 0, with every constant explicit, set by the fast contraction rate λ_z, the reduced contraction rate λ_x and the manifold's drift. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-294](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-294.md) | When a network's architecture can represent a structured system's renormalization step exactly, must training by distribution fitting make the variables it represents the system's relevant ones? | The representability part of [QUESTION-060](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-060.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-197.md) (Active) settles it, in the negative. Mehta and Schwab's RBM–renormalization correspondence is an identity of parametrizations, and an exact RG step is a perfect fit of the data distribution. Away from that point a contrastive-divergence RBM spends its hidden units on noise, not on the relevant fields. The architecture's match does not fix what training keeps. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md) | When the effects of trauma reach descendants who did not live through it, by which route do they travel: germline epigenetics, the womb, parenting, or a group's narrative and identity; and on the identity route, does an ancestor's injury become part of the descendant's self? | The owner's question of 2026-10-29, beside the legacy line: the past acting on later generations, where legacy is the living acting for them. Claims of epigenetic transmission of trauma rest on animal work (Dias and Ressler) and small human studies (Yehuda et al.), against a sceptical consensus that mammalian germline reprogramming blocks it. Meta-analyses find little general second- or third-generation harm among Holocaust survivors' descendants. On the cultural route, a group's past injury becomes part of its identity (chosen trauma, cultural trauma), which is the owner's extended self running backward in time. | Open |
